title: One-sided negative sectional curvature and the holomorphic Liouville property
main_claim: For some finite m there is a domain T in C^m, diffeomorphic to R^{2m}, carrying a complete Kähler metric with Sec <= -1 (unbounded below) and H^infty(T)=C. This answers Yau's one-sided bounded-holomorphic-function question in the negative. The construction is a tube {Im w > l(s,y)} over a complete nonpositively curved Kähler potential l on C^{n+1}, built by a fiber Legendre transform with polynomial wells and sheared testing disks.

issues.location: Sections 5, 7 and 8 (quiet profile, center change, trigger/reset lemmas)
issues.description: Many steps end with assertions like 'fits the quiet raw exponent' or 'pays all these estimates' that pack several exponent comparisons into one sentence. I spot-checked the leading exponents and they are consistent, but I did not re-derive every budget inequality line by line. This is a limit on verification, not a demonstrated gap.
issues.evidence: e.g. 08-assembly.tex Lemma assembly:quiet-check ('The trigger cost e^{4E/k_b} fits the quiet raw exponent'), Lemma assembly:post, Lemma assembly:reset; the choices of B_*, C_*, epsilon_1 in eq. assembly:second-constants are meant to absorb them.

coverage:
Read in full and checked: Section 1, Section 2 (tube transfer and corollary), Section 3 (grid lemma, phase lemma, extraction, criterion), Section 4 (Legendre metric, six blocks, rank-two absorption, perturbation identity), Section 6 start (radial ODEs, radial curvature), and all of Section 8 (assembly, exponents, disks, completeness).

Checks that passed:
- Tube transfer: the 3-jet normalization by holomorphic coordinates and the w-shift; the curvature difference equals b^{-1} times the base curvature; the model value Sec = -1-3β² in [-4,-1].
- Grid lemma: sphere-bound exponents (C_n=8n); inverse-Jacobian bound N^9 and shell bound N^{-39}/2 >= N^{-40}; lift radii.
- Phase lemma: rank fraction < .02; mean >= .38 t_h²; Gram-matrix variance bounded by rank/M².
- Criterion: extraction ratio <= e^{-.99c/N}; exponent ε = min(m0-p1, .99k-p0-p1, .99); three-lines step with D_j/c_j -> 0.
- Assembly bookkeeping: node log-radius >= (d - d/8 - d/16)c = 13d/16·c > m0 = d/2; sphere exponent about 1.19d < p0 = 2d; p1 <= d/4; the shear is cancelled exactly by the holomorphic w-shift; height bound uses l(s,ζ)=B(s) on the center axis.
- Numerical: all six curvature blocks (A, A_i, W, spin, K, L) and the Schur complement h of Lemma 4.2, checked against a direct Kähler curvature computation on an explicit example (q = 1/(1+k(s)τ), Lambert-W inverse, n=1, tilted frame). They agree to about 1e-16.
- Numerical: radial curvature components (2, κ, D=κ(1+κ+Yκ_Y)), checked by sympy.
- Rank-two absorption constants (1.5-408η² >= 1) and the 5/9 radial reserve.

Sections 5 and 7 (the detailed quiet-profile and center-change estimates) were only skimmed via their use in Section 8.
